answer: Rhythm-Gated Admission. Each identity must emit a minimum number of transactions over a randomized window before its traffic counts toward quorum, and the scheduler caps early bursts so a fresh clone looks hollow during that warm-up. A single hollow clone can harbor many parallel tasks, but each admitted identity still pays the fixed delay and booking cost per slot, so mass cloning multiplies waiting time and fees rather than amortizing them. The signal is the arrival curve itself: steady, aged traffic unlocks rights; bursty newborn traffic stays throttled.
